title: Multitenant KV isolation: noisy-neighbor load-scan for hit-rate vs p95 vs memory
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Build and run a multitenant "noisy neighbor" load-scan harness that characterizes how prefix/KV cache hit-rate, tail latency (p95/p99) and memory footprint interact under mixed-tenancy scenarios. Produce a small regression detector that flags >10% p95 regression or >8% hit-rate drop compared to baseline for given memory budgets. Deliverables: workload generator, measurement dashboard, analysis notebook, and an automated CI job that runs a reduced sweep on each runtime change.
steps: Design workload mixes: 3 tenant profiles (short-prefix chat, long-context completion, embedding-heavy) with configurable proportions
Implement multitenant harness: spawn N simulated tenants on a single KV shard using existing kvcache test harness (extend to support tenant IDs and eviction isolation flags)
Define memory budgets: run sweeps at 2GB, 6GB, 12GB per shard and with LRU/segmented policies
Measure metrics: tokens/sec aggregate, tokens/sec per tenant, p50/p95/p99 latency per tenant, kv hit-rate per tenant, total RSS and slab fragmentation
Introduce adversarial bursts: periodic 30s hotkey storms at 10x normal token rate to simulate spikes
Capture traces and KV eviction events and push to the perf dashboard
Create a regression detector: baseline is median of 5 clean runs; regression if p95 increases >10% or hit-rate drops >8% under same mem budget
Run full sweep on bench env and record phase-diagram plots (hit-rate vs p95 vs memory) and a multitenant interference heatmap
Document results and recommended guardrails (per-tenant cache quotas, eviction isolation knobs, autoscale triggers)
Add a nightly CI micro-sweep that runs a trimmed set of scenarios and posts results to perf-alert Slack channel
workload_profiles: Profile A: Short-prefix chat — mean seq len 64, burstiness 2x, high prefix reuse (target hit-rate high)
Profile B: Long completions — mean seq len 1024, low repeat prefixes, steady tokens/sec
Profile C: Embedding/metadata activity — many small requests, low token count but high request rate, low KV locality
environment_config: bench_cluster: 3x A100 nodes, same runtime build as CI (runtime-1.21-beta)
kv_shard_config: single shard with tenant isolation flags configurable
network: intra-rack latency simulated with netem 0-1ms
observability: perf traces -> perf-prod Grafana; histograms exported to bench-s3
seeding: workload generator uses request traces from production-sampled dataset (anonymized)
acceptance_criteria: Harness exists and can run the three profile mixes concurrently and reproduce baseline within ±5% for tokens/sec and ±7% for p95
Phase-diagram (hit-rate vs p95 vs memory) generated for each tenant mix and committed to confluence
Regression detector implemented; alerts on PRs if trimmed nightly sweep shows regression against baseline
Recommendations for runtime knobs (cache quota suggestions and autoscale triggers) drafted and reviewed by runtime owners
Performance dashboard with heatmaps and downloadable CSVs is available at the bench dashboard link
